abstract: Diabetes mellitus comprises a group of highly heterogeneous diseases that differ in pathogenic mechanisms and clinical phenotypes, for which traditional classification systems fall short of meeting the demands of precision diagnosis and treatment. Recent genomic studies have uncovered the distinct genetic backgrounds of different diabetes subtypes, driving the development of novel classification tools such as genetic risk scores. Owing to its stability, inherent accessibility, and lifelong applicability, genetic information serves as an important complement to existing diagnostic systems. This expert forum discusses recent advances in the application of genetic factors to diabetes classification, highlighting the translational value of genomics from genes to clinical practice and offering new perspectives for individualized precision medicine.
